education.degree: Bachelor of Science in Computer Science

summary.text: Software Engineer at Harbor Systems building a booking platform in TypeScript and Node.js, after an internship building React web apps. Also builds backend services in Go through personal projects.

points.text: Built the booking flow for a travel platform used by partner hotels, as one of four engineers.

variants.text: Built the booking flow for a travel platform used by partner hotels with React, Node.js and REST APIs, as one of four engineers.

points.text: Cut the booking page's load time from about 4.2 seconds to 1.8 by splitting the app and caching hotel data, together with the backend team.

variants.text: Cut the booking page's load time from about 4.2 seconds to 1.8 by code splitting and caching hotel data in Redis, together with the backend team.

points.text: Designed the retry and error screens so a failed payment never leaves a guest unsure whether they were charged.
Replaced polling with live availability updates, so a room that sells out disappears for other guests within seconds.

variants.text: Replaced polling with WebSocket updates, so a room that sells out disappears for other guests within seconds.

points.text: Wrote the runbooks and dashboards the four-person team uses to watch bookings, so a failing payment provider is noticed within minutes instead of the next morning.
Built responsive dashboards for the agency's clients with React and Tailwind CSS.
Connected the dashboards to REST APIs with consistent loading and error states.
Split the dashboard code so each report loads only when opened.

variants.text: Used code splitting and lazy loading so each report loads only when opened.

points.text: Rebuilt the studio client sites on a shared component library, so a design change reaches every site in one release instead of a week of copy and paste.
Added automated browser tests for the contact and checkout forms, which caught two broken releases before clients saw them.
Moved image delivery to a resizing service, cutting page weight on photo-heavy sites by about half.
Built a message queue with an HTTP API for publishing, claiming and acknowledging messages across named queues.
Leased each claimed message for a set time and requeued it if unacknowledged, so a stalled consumer's message is delivered again.
Moved messages that failed three deliveries to a dead-letter list so they stop retrying, and exposed per-queue counts.

variants.text: Moved messages that failed three deliveries to a dead-letter queue (DLQ) so they stop retrying, and exposed per-queue counts.

projects.title: Team Chat
projects.stack: Next.js, React, Node.js, TypeScript, Redis, PostgreSQL

points.text: Built a team chat app end to end, with channels, roles, invite links and direct messages.
Separated live delivery from saving, so the database can fall behind without slowing the live feed.
Made the storage worker pause and resume after a failed write instead of crash-looping on one bad message.
Built a gateway that routes each tenant's traffic to its services, with roles and API keys managed through an admin API.
Applied rate limits separately to each tenant and paused requests to failing services before probing for recovery.

variants.text: Applied rate limiting separately to each tenant and added a circuit breaker that pauses requests to failing services before probing for recovery.

points.text: Recorded API usage in the background, dropping and counting overflow instead of slowing requests down.
Built a scraper that collects public job listings from several boards and stores each posting once, whichever board it came from.
Detected reposted listings by comparing company, title and location, so the same job is never shown twice with a new date.
Backed off automatically when a board slowed down, so the scraper stays polite and is never blocked for hammering a site.
Built a notes service with sharing links, tags and full-text search behind a documented REST API for a small team.
Cached the most read notes and cleared the cache on every edit, so readers never see an old version of a note.
Added per-user request limits and clear error messages so a script that misbehaves cannot slow the service for everyone else.
Built a public status page that shows the health of each service and updates live without a refresh.
Kept the page readable when many services fail at once by grouping incidents instead of listing every alert.
Sent a short email when a service stays down for more than five minutes, and a second one when it recovers.
